title: If a Stock Market Crash Comes in November, You'll Rest Easy Owning This 50-Year Dividend King
detail:
If a Stock Market Crash Comes in November, You'll Rest Easy Owning This 50-Year Dividend King
Jennifer Saibil, The Motley Fool
Wed, November 4, 2026 at 1:20 PM MST 4 min read
WMT
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Is a stock market crash on the way? The short answer to that is yes, because it's bound to happen at some point. The longer answer is more complicated, because there are signs it could happen soon, but it's unknown.

Long-term investors know that a crash is part and parcel of investing, and new investors shouldn't get too excited about soaring artificial intelligence (AI) stocks. While you should certainly have top growth stocks in your portfolio, you should always be prepared for the prospect, or eventuality, of a market crash.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

If it happens this month, Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT) is an excellent defensive stock to protect your portfolio.

Why Walmart?

Walmart is the largest supermarket chain in the U.S., and since it's a discount retailer, it's many shoppers' main stop for essentials. That means it can generate increasing revenue in any kind of economy, and it often does even better in tough economies, when customers who might shop at more expensive stores switch to save money.

Image source: Walmart.

One of the advantages it has over other supermarkets is its store count. Including Walmart and Sam's Club stores, its warehouse membership chain, it has more than 5,700 stores in the U.S., and one of them is within 10 miles of 90% of the population.

But it reaches the entire population through its robust digital channels. It's the second-largest e-commerce retailer behind Amazon, and it recently increased its market share. According to Statista, it has 9.2%, a distant second to Amazon's 40.5%. However, Walmart's e-commerce division is actually growing much faster than Amazon's. E-commerce sales increased 23% year over year in the 2027 fiscal second quarter (ended July 31), and 24% in the U.S. It was the 10th consecutive quarter of U.S. e-commerce growth higher than 20%. Amazon's third-quarter online sales were up 2%, and third-party sales were up 9%.

Here Walmart's stores play a role, too. They act as distribution hubs to deliver to customers quickly without incurring build-out costs, and they also offer varied options, such as in-store pickup.

What might happen as inflation soars?

Walmart stock is up a respectable 12% year-to-date, in line with the S&P 500. However, investors have been concerned about the impact of inflation.

Remember, though, that customers come to Walmart for its low prices. So while the short term can look choppy, the trend is in Walmart's favor.

A broad shift in U.S. stocks followed the midterm elections Wednesday, with investors buying shares across several industries as the new balance of power in Washington came into focus.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 1,200 points, or 2.3%, in Wednesday trading. The S&P 500 rose 1.8%, while the Nasdaq Composite added 2%.

Democrats secured control of the House and Senate, setting up a divided government that could make major policy changes harder to push through. President Donald Trump's willingness to accept the results helped calm concerns about a possible political confrontation.

Some parts of the market moved in the opposite direction. CoreWeave and other data center-related companies faced pressure amid concerns that a new political leadership in Texas could create obstacles for infrastructure projects. West Texas Intermediate crude also declined about 3%, offering some relief on the inflation front.

title: Walmart's Dec. 11 Dividend Isn't the Real Reason to Own the Stock
detail:
Walmart's Dec. 11 Dividend Isn't the Real Reason to Own the Stock
Jack Delaney, The Motley Fool
Wed, November 4, 2026 at 9:50 AM MST 5 min read
WMT
NVDA
KO
PG
NKE
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

For shareholders of record as of Dec. 11, Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT) will pay out a dividend of $0.24 per share on Jan. 4, 2027. For current shareholders, it's a nice way to ring in a new year with some income.

That said, the payout, which yields 0.8%, doesn't offer much incentive in and of itself for anyone who doesn't own shares to go out and buy some before Dec. 11. Just within the consumer goods sector, higher yields are available through Coca-Cola (2.2%), Procter & Gamble (2.6%), and Nike (4.2%).

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Still, even with that lower yield, there's a reason why Walmart stock is worth owning.

Image source: The Motley Fool.
The strong business model

While Walmart's dividend yield is on the low side, there's more to it than just a percentage. What's most important is the number of years the retail giant has consecutively increased its dividend payout: 53. By increasing those payouts for 50 or more consecutive years, Walmart has earned the title of Dividend King.

To earn that title, you need a strong business model, as over the last 50 years, Walmart has dealt with stagflation, inflation, war, economic slumps, technological disruptions, and plenty else that's been thrown at it. Still, it's kept increasing the dividend it pays to its shareholders year in and year out.

And that strong business model, which has enabled so many consecutive dividend payout increases, is why Walmart is worth considering as an investment. Plus, as Walmart leans more into technological advancements that make the shopping experience easier and can also generate additional sales, its business model is becoming more robust than ever.

Tapping into the powers of technology

With artificial intelligence (AI), there's a lot of debate on whether it's adding real value to businesses. For instance, as prolific as the rise of AI has seemed, according to research from The Motley Fool, only 24.6% of businesses in the United States were using it in October 2026.

That said, not only is Walmart finding use cases for it, but it's actually a case study on how AI is helping increase sales. For its fiscal 2027 second-quarter earnings, the company reported that the number of customers who used its AI shopping agent, Sparky, was up 70% from the prior-year period. In addition, customers who used it to shop spent 40% more per order than those who didn't.

Angi (NASDAQ:ANGI) reported third-quarter revenue of $242 million, down 8.9% from a year earlier, while adjusted EBITDA rose 6.3% to $42.2 million as the home-services marketplace reduced fixed expenses and tightened marketing spending.

New CEO Mike Steib, who recently joined the company, said Angi is building from a more stable base after several years of declining service requests and leads. Demand and Marketplace Metrics

Angi said third-quarter service requests declined 2.4% year over year to roughly 4 million, an improvement from a 5.5% decline in the prior quarter. Average pro capacity increased in the low double digits, partially offsetting the reduction in active pros, while total pro capacity declined in the mid-single digits. Revenue per lead rose 9.8% to $47 as Angi exited the discounted legacy advertising product and increased its mix of larger pros.

title: Is Dollar General Stock a Buy at Its Current Valuation?
detail:
Is Dollar General Stock a Buy at Its Current Valuation?
Sumit Singh

DG
WMT
COST
^GSPC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Dollar General Corporation DG has drawn investor attention as improving business performance, stronger customer traffic and strategic growth initiatives reinforce its long-term prospects. The discount retailer's focus on everyday affordability, store enhancements, merchandising improvements and expanding digital capabilities has supported its growth momentum. However, persistent cost pressures and a challenging consumer environment remain concerns. Against this backdrop, investors may be wondering whether DG's current valuation presents an attractive buying opportunity or already reflects its improving fundamentals.

DG currently trades at a forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 15.74, a discount to the industry average of 28.89 and the S&P 500's 18.55. The stock also trades well below Walmart Inc. WMT and Costco Wholesale Corporation COST, which command forward 12-month P/E multiples of 39.77 and 44.13, respectively. DG's current multiple is also below its 12-month median P/E of 16.09, indicating that the stock is trading marginally above its recent historical valuation despite its discount to peers.

While DG's relatively lower valuation may appeal to value-conscious investors, does it offer sufficient upside potential? Let's take a closer look.

Dollar General Valuation Picture
Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

How Has Dollar General Stock Fared Lately?

Shares of Dollar General have gained a modest 2.8% over the past three months compared with the industry's rise of 1.9%. The stock has underperformed Walmart and Costco, which have advanced 10.4% and 7.6%, respectively, during the same period. This relatively subdued performance raises the question of whether DG's business fundamentals can support stronger investor confidence and drive further upside.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Dollar General's Growth Drivers and Strategic Initiatives

Dollar General's strong value proposition and extensive neighborhood presence continue to drive customer traffic and market share gains. Its everyday low-price strategy, convenient locations and targeted promotions resonate with budget-conscious shoppers while attracting middle- and higher-income consumers seeking greater affordability. The growing popularity of its Value Valley assortment and strategic pricing investments enhance its competitive positioning. Sustained demand across consumable and non-consumable categories reinforces prospects for continued sales growth.

DG is strengthening its non-consumable offerings through trend-focused merchandise, licensed products and refreshed assortments, helping attract shoppers and support a more favorable sales mix. Meanwhile, its Project Renovate and Project Elevate programs are enhancing existing stores through upgraded layouts, expanded cooler capacity, refreshed product adjacencies and improved merchandise presentations. These initiatives are designed to elevate the shopping experience, encourage incremental purchases and drive comparable-sales growth. Management targets annualized comparable-sales lifts of about 6% for Project Renovate and 3% for Project Elevate stores.

Dollar General's expanding store footprint provides another avenue for long-term growth. Its ongoing expansion strategy is designed to attract new customers, deepen market penetration and extend its reach into underserved communities. The retailer is also refining its store formats to incorporate broader assortments, expanded cooler capacity and enhanced health and beauty offerings, allowing it to better address local customer preferences. DG's measured expansion in Mexico offers additional opportunities to extend its value-and-convenience proposition into new markets. The company plans to open approximately 450 U.S. stores and 10 additional locations in Mexico during fiscal 2026. DG is also pursuing store simplification, private-brand development and artificial intelligence-enabled workflows to improve productivity and manage costs.

The company's expanding digital ecosystem is creating incremental revenue opportunities while enhancing shopping convenience and customer accessibility. Its myDG Delivery platform, alongside partnerships with DoorDash and Uber Eats, enables customers to shop beyond traditional store visits, with delivery orders generally generating larger baskets than in-store transactions. Meanwhile, DG Media Network is broadening advertising opportunities through sponsored products, improved search capabilities, connected television, social media and in-store media offerings. Management's continued focus on scaling delivery, personalizing digital engagement and expanding advertising capabilities should strengthen customer relationships.

Trading disclosure

Dollar General Corporation DG is gaining traction with its Value Valley assortment as budget-conscious shoppers prioritize affordability. Built around rotating merchandise at a fixed $1 price point, the offering reinforces the retailer's everyday-value proposition. With persistent inflation and volatile fuel prices straining household budgets, low-priced products could remain attractive to consumers seeking to stretch their spending.

Value Valley now features more than 600 rotating items, each priced at $1. In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, the assortment recorded comparable-sales growth exceeding 16%, well above the company's overall comparable-sales growth of 3.5%.

The retailer also expanded its $1 off-shelf displays in more than 9,000 stores during the quarter. Management indicated that these stores were generating greater incremental comparable-sales growth than the rest of the chain, suggesting that more prominent placement is helping customers discover and purchase the assortment. Across its broader merchandise offering, Dollar General carries more than 2,000 items priced at or below $1.

Management plans to broaden the presence of $1 products in fall and holiday assortments. This could give customers more reasons to browse Value Valley. With customer demand surging and continuous optimization of low-priced assortments, the Value Valley concept provides substantial runway for sustained sales growth and enhanced customer engagement moving forward.

How Does Dollar General Stack Up Against Its Industry?

Dollar General, which competes with Walmart Inc. WMT and Target Corporation TGT, has seen its shares advance 2.8% over the past three months compared with the industry's rise of 1.9%. While shares of Walmart have gained 10.4%, those of Target have jumped 4.5% during the same period.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

What Does Dollar General's Current Valuation Suggest?

From a valuation standpoint, Dollar General's forward 12-month price-to-earnings ratio stands at 15.74, lower than the industry's 28.89. The stock is also trading below its 12-month median level of 16.09. Dollar General trades below Walmart's multiple of 39.77 but broadly in line with Target's 15.88.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

What Do Earnings Estimates Signal for Dollar General?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Dollar General's current fiscal-year sales and earnings per share implies year-over-year growth of 5.8% and 15.9%, respectively. For the next fiscal year, the consensus estimate indicates sales growth of 4.2% and earnings growth of 5.8%.
